topics.title: Variables, Values & Types
topics.summary: Store and inspect data with let and const, recognize JavaScript primitive values, and understand that variables have values while values have types.

concepts.name: let and const
concepts.explanation: Use const when a binding should not be reassigned and let when reassignment is part of the design. Avoid var in new beginner code until you understand its older scoping rules.

concepts.name: Primitive values
concepts.explanation: Common primitive types are string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, symbol, and null. Objects are the major non-primitive category.

concepts.name: Dynamic typing
concepts.explanation: A JavaScript variable is not permanently locked to one value type. typeof helps inspect many values, but null is a famous historical edge case because typeof null is "object".

topics.challenge: Declare a const name, a mutable numeric score/health variable, change the number, and log both values.
topics.hint: Use const for the name and let for the value you intend to reassign.

topics.title: Operators, Conditions & Boolean Logic
topics.summary: Combine expressions with arithmetic, comparison, logical operators, and if/switch control flow.

concepts.name: Comparisons
concepts.explanation: Prefer strict equality === and !== for predictable comparisons. Relational operators such as <, >, <=, and >= compare ordered values.

concepts.name: Boolean logic
concepts.explanation: && requires both sides to be truthy, || chooses when at least one side is truthy, and ! negates a truthy/falsy result.

concepts.name: Branches
concepts.explanation: if/else is flexible for arbitrary conditions. switch is useful when one expression is matched against many known cases.

topics.challenge: Write a condition that prints Pass when a score is at least 80 and Retry otherwise.
topics.hint: Your condition should compare the score with 80 using >=.

topics.title: Loops & Arrays
topics.summary: Store ordered values in arrays and repeat work with for, for...of, while, and array indexing.

concepts.name: Arrays
concepts.explanation: Arrays are ordered, zero-indexed collections. length tells you how many entries exist, and methods such as push/pop modify the end.

concepts.name: for and while
concepts.explanation: for is convenient when setup, condition, and update fit together. while is useful when repetition depends on a condition rather than a known count.

concepts.name: for...of
concepts.explanation: for...of reads iterable values directly and is often clearer than manual indexing when you only need each value.

topics.challenge: Create an array with at least three values and print every value using a loop.
topics.hint: for...of is the simplest choice when you do not need the array index.

topics.title: Functions, Parameters & Scope
topics.summary: Package behavior into reusable functions, pass data through parameters, return results, and reason about where names are visible.

concepts.name: Function contracts
concepts.explanation: Parameters describe inputs and return describes the output. A focused function should have a clear purpose that can be described in one sentence.

concepts.name: Function forms
concepts.explanation: Function declarations, function expressions, and arrow functions all create callable values, but they differ in details such as hoisting and this behavior.

concepts.name: Scope
concepts.explanation: let and const are block scoped. Names declared inside a function are normally unavailable outside it; inner scopes can access names from outer scopes.

topics.challenge: Write a function that accepts two numbers, returns a calculated result, and log the returned value.
topics.hint: Put the reusable calculation inside the function and use return rather than logging only inside the function.

topics.title: DOM Selection & Events
topics.summary: Connect JavaScript to HTML by selecting elements, changing content/classes, and responding to user events.

concepts.name: Selecting elements
concepts.explanation: querySelector returns the first matching element; querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList of matches. Check for null when a selector may not find anything.

concepts.name: Updating the DOM
concepts.explanation: textContent changes text safely, classList manages classes, and createElement/append can build new nodes without composing raw HTML strings.

concepts.name: Events
concepts.explanation: addEventListener registers behavior without overwriting other listeners. Event objects describe what happened and which target was involved.

topics.challenge: Select a button and another element, then update the second element when the button is clicked.
topics.hint: Use querySelector twice, then attach a click listener with addEventListener.
